description.value: A forested creek-side campground on Williams Creek at the edge of Barkerville Historic Town, western North America's largest living history museum; flush toilets, coin showers, and potable water on site, though cyclists must push bikes through the heritage townsite itself. Open mid-May to late September only.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The Barkerville website campgrounds page provides strong primary evidence for Forest Rose Campground: potable water, coin-operated showers, flush toilets, bear-proof food storage, and advance reservations are all explicitly confirmed. OSM tags (drinking_water=yes, shower=yes, reservation=yes, power_supply=yes) are fully corroborated by the website. Contact details (phone and address) are absent in OSM but found on the website's contact page, so contact_confirmed fields for those are null (no OSM value to compare against).
concerns: OSM record has no phone or address; phone (1-888-994-3332 ext. 99) and mailing address (Box 19, 14301 Highway 26 East, Barkerville, BC V0K 1B0) sourced from website contact page only.
Cyclists should be aware that bicycles must be walked through the Barkerville Heritage Zone townsite and are not permitted on the boardwalks per the visitor information page.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Legitimate, well-documented operational campground with confirmed water, showers, and bear-proof storage at a major BC heritage destination; a clear asset for touring cyclists passing through the Cariboo.
enrichment_extras.notes: OSM power_supply=yes is corroborated by website listing 30-amp electrical hookup sites, but no dedicated device-charging station for cyclists is mentioned. The campground is managed by Barkerville Heritage Trust on behalf of the Province of BC.

wow_evidence: western North America's largest living history museum
